rationale:
The reviewed tests cover every obligation of `requirements.sdk.outlines.selection`, and their assertions enforce the expected outcomes. I did not request any implementation source. The mapping below is what I checked.

**Resolving a selector against the retained outline and returning an owned `OutlineContent`**
- `rust_items_attach_documentation_and_preserve_structural_hashes` selects every outline item by its selector. Each result's `text()` equals the item's source span, and its `structural_hash()` equals the item's hash. It also selects a nested item (`mod[auth]/fn[check]`) and the empty root selector.
- `markdown_heading_levels_resolve_encoded_duplicates_and_anonymous_items` selects nested sections, `#N` duplicates, percent-encoded names, and anonymous `section@` and `block@` items. It checks the returned text for each.
- `css_duplicate_names_are_numbered_after_normalization_within_each_parent` selects `#N` duplicates, including ones nested under a parent.
- `unicode_spans_use_bytes_and_whitespace_only_lines_create_no_items` selects `line@` items and checks the text, including multi-byte text.
- `selected_contents_outlive_handles_and_later_file_edits` checks `id()` and `text()` on selected contents.

**Sharing the original snapshot and fingerprinting rules**
- `std::ptr::eq(second.outline(), contents.outline())` and `std::ptr::eq(function.outline(), contents.outline())` show the selected handle shares the retained outline.
- `explicit_languages_share_configuration_and_retain_their_scheme` checks that the selected contents keep the custom scheme (`custom-v2`) after the language and scheme are dropped. It also checks that a different scheme (`custom-v3`) gives a different fingerprint for the same structural hash.
- The Rust test compares fingerprints for reformatted and changed sources.

**No additional file read, and usability after the original handle is dropped**
- `selected_contents_outlive_handles_and_later_file_edits` drops `file` and rewrites the file on disk. It then checks that `selected` keeps its original fingerprint and text.
- The same test calls `selected.select("")` after the edit. The result still holds the original `"first\nsecond\n"`, with the root id, while a fresh `from_id` fails. This shows no re-read happens.

**Selector syntax applied, including interchangeable identical lines**
- `ambiguous_items_are_errors_except_for_identical_plain_text_lines` selects a duplicated `line@` selector and gets the text `"same"`.
- `unknown_extensions_keep_nonblank_lines_and_content_selectors` selects by the shared `line@` selector.
- The percent-encoding, `#N`, `kind@hash`, and empty-selector cases are covered by the Markdown, CSS, and Rust tests above.

**Invalid, missing, and ambiguous selections return errors**
- `missing_file_and_invalid_selections_are_errors` checks that the malformed selector `fn[` and the missing item `fn[absent]` both return errors.
- `ambiguous_items_are_errors_except_for_identical_plain_text_lines` checks that duplicate `part[same]` items return an error whose message contains "ambiguous". It also checks that duplicate `line` items with differing hashes return an ambiguity error.
- The CSS test asserts that the un-numbered `rule[a%20b]` errors when `#1` and `#2` exist.

**Original text before redaction**
- `formatted_contents_redact_credentials_while_retaining_raw_text_and_spans` checks that the selected item's `text()` still contains the raw token while `format()` is redacted.

I found no obligation of this requirement without a test and assertion. Further malformed-selector shapes, such as an out-of-range `#N`, are edge cases the text does not name. They are not gaps.

text: :::{req} selection
`OutlineContent::select` resolves a selector from the file's root against the
retained outline. It returns another owned `OutlineContent` for that item,
sharing the original source snapshot and fingerprinting rules. Selection
performs no additional file read and remains usable after the original handle
is dropped. Resolution follows
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax`, including its rule that
identical plain-text lines are interchangeable. Invalid, missing, or ambiguous
selections return an error under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.errors`.
```rust,ignore
impl OutlineContent {
/// Select an item from this retained file snapshot.
pub fn select(&self, selector: &str) -> Result<Self, OutlineError>;
/// Address of the selected item.
pub fn id(&self) -> &OutlineId;
/// Original selected text, including attached source, before redaction.
pub fn text(&self) -> &str;
:::{req} selector_syntax
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
:::{req} errors
The outline API makes a best effort to recover from parse errors.
File-read and unrecoverable parsing failures return errors, distinct from
successful contents for an empty file. Selecting a language commits to that
language's parsing rules.
A malformed selector, a missing item, or an ambiguity not permitted by
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax` also returns an error.
